## 1\. USERS & GROUPS

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| USER | An account on the Linux machine. |
| GROUP | A collection of users who can share permissions. |
| groupadd developers | Create a group. |
| usermod \-aG developers ahmed | Add Ahmed to the developers group. |
| groups ahmed | See what groups Ahmed belongs to. |
| getent group developers | See the developers group and its members. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: Groups make it easier to manage access for many users at once.* |  |

## 2\. PERMISSIONS

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| Categories | OWNER | GROUP | OTHERS |
| r, w, x | read (4), write (2), execute (1) |
| 7, 6, 5, 4, 0 | rwx, rw-, r-x, r--, \--- |
| chmod 770 /project | Owner=rwx, Group=rwx, Others=--- |
| chgrp developers /project | Change the group assigned to /project. |
| ls \-ld /project | Check folder's owner, group, and permissions. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: LEAST PRIVILEGE \- Only give people the access they actually need.* |  |

## 3\. PROCESSES

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| PROCESS / PID | A program running / Process ID (unique number). |
| sleep 300 | Start a process that sleeps for 300 seconds. |
| ps aux | Show running processes. |
| ps aux | grep sleep | Search the process list for "sleep". |
| kill \[PID\] | Stop/terminate the process with the given PID. |
| Ctrl \+ C | Stop a command currently running in the terminal. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: Useful for troubleshooting and security investigations to know what is running.* |  |

## 4\. NETWORKING

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| ip \-br addr | Show network interfaces and IP addresses. |
| 127.0.0.1 | LOCALHOST \= the machine itself. |
| ping \[IP\] | Test communication with self, VM, or external IPs. |
| Ping Results | Packets transmitted, received, and packet loss. |
| Ping Failure | Doesn't mean offline; could be firewall, routing, etc. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: Helps diagnose network connectivity issues.* |  |

## 5\. PORTS & SERVICES

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| PORT / SERVICE | Network entry point / Program listening for connections. |
| ss \-tuln | Show listening network ports. |
| ss \-tulnp | Show listening ports \+ associated processes. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: Helps you see what your machine is listening for.* |  |

## 6\. ECHO & FILE REDIRECTION

| Command/Concept | Description/Details |
| ----- | ----- |
| echo "text" | Display "text" in the terminal. |
| echo "text" \> file | Put "text" into file (OVERWRITES contents). |
| echo "text" \>\> file | Add "text" to END of file (APPENDS contents). |
| cat file | Display the contents of file. |
| *WHY IT MATTERS: Lets you save command output and modify files for automation.* |  |

# fundamentals

* **Motherboard** connects all components and holds them in place such as CPU socket, RAM slots, expansion slots, and various ports.  
  &nbsp;  
* **CPU (central processing unit**) is like the brain, connects to motherboard via CPU socket  
  &nbsp;  
* **RAM (random access memory)** is like short term memory. It holds the data that the CPU needs quick access to and it is volatile so if all power is lost, all contents are gone.  
  &nbsp;  
* **SSD’s and HDD’s** are like long term memory. HDD’s use older tech with moving parts and limiting performance while SSD have no moving parts and use memory chips which makes it faster. HDDs are popular for their large capacity at low cost. Storage would connect through SATA cables or PCI express slots.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Network adapters** let computers communicate with other systems.. Usually they're connected to motherboards and they can also be added as expansion cards connected through PCI express ports.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **PSU (power supply)** supplies energy to all system components. If components need more power than the PSU can give, the system will fail. It gets power from the outlet and gives it to various connectors like the motherboard.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **Graphics Card** is like the visual cortex of the brain, it receives info from operating systems and programs then outputs processed visual data to a monitor. They connect to PCI express slots on the motherboard.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **Input/output.** For input there are keyboards, mics, mice, scanners. Output devices include monitor, printer, and speakers. Common connectors include HDMI, USB, display port.  
  &nbsp;  
* **IoT** devices are network connected devices with a single purpose like objects such as thermostats, smart doorbells, fitness trackers.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Embedded** computer is a computer built into another device like coffee maker controller, automatic door sensor, lamp  
  &nbsp;  
* A **Port** is used to identify a specific service running on a system. When a client wants to access a service on a server, it must connect using the correct port.  
  &nbsp;  
* **DNS** (domain name system) is when you enter the name of a website, DNS resolves it to the server's location. Location coordinates are called **internet protocol** **IP** addresses.  
  &nbsp;  
* **HTTP** (hyper transfer protocol) is a client server protocol used for the world wide web. Which means each request is processed independently without the server retaining info about old requests.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# Deployment types

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

* **Public cloud \-** used by startups, sites, global apps cuz its affordable, easy to scale.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Private cloud \-** used by banks, healthcare, and government organizations cuz it offers greater control.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Hybrid cloud \-** used by companies like ecommerce platforms that need to keep sensitive data private while still scaling publicly during high demand.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)**: You rent basic computing power like servers and storage, but you handle the software running on them.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Platform as a Service (PaaS)**: The provider takes care of the servers and operating system, so you can just focus on building and running your app.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Software as a Service (SaaS)**: You use a complete app online, like Gmail, and the provider manages everything behind the scenes.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Elastic compute cloud (EC2)** Amazon’s cloud computers that you can quickly create, use, and resize whenever you need them.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Virtualization** allows multiple applications to share the same physical server resources making it more efficient and cost effective.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Hypervisor** is a virtualization layer that acts like a referee between lab machines and allows each virtual computer to behave independently like a physical computer.  
  &nbsp;  
* **A lab machine** is a virtual computer created by the hypervisor. It has its own virtual cpu, ram, storage, networks and can run on any operating system like windows and linux etc.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Containers** are packages of software that bundle up code, and consistently run on different systems.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **Container images** is the pre-packed template used to create containers.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Network ports** are special numbered entry points that apps use to talk over the network.  
  &nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
  &nbsp;

&nbsp;

# active machines info

* **Operating system** is the core software that manages hardware, applications and all system resources.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **Kernel space** is a part of the OS where the kernel runs. It has direct access to hardware like CPU, memory, devices etc. and control system resources for the whole computer.  
  &nbsp;  
* **User space** is the area where regular apps run with limited permissions for safety and system stability.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
* **Graphical user interface (GUI)** the visual part of the OS, windows icon, and menus that lets you interact through clicking and tapping. (the one with icons)  
  &nbsp;  
* **Command line interface (CLI)** is a text based interface where you type commands to control the system with precision and speed. (the one with weird hacking text like the homebrew chanel wii)  
  &nbsp;

&nbsp;

# operating systems basics

* **Windows security** is the central dashboard for managing windows built in security tools  
  &nbsp;  
* **Windows Defender firewall** is the firewall designed to help protect your system from unauthorized network traffic.

# Data representation

* **Decimal (Base-10) system**: This is the system we use in our everyday life.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Binary (Base-2) system**: Computers understand two states, which are encoded as 0 and 1\.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Hexadecimal (Base-16) system**: Every 4 binary digits (bits) can be grouped as one hexadecimal digit. A hexadecimal digit ranges between 0 and F.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Octal (Base-8) system**: Every 3 binary digits (bits) can be grouped as one octal digit. An octal digit ranges between 0 and 7\. This one is less commonly encountered on computer systems.

&nbsp;

  &nbsp;

* **Bit**: It is short for binary digit, and it can be either 0 or 1\.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Byte**: On modern systems, a byte is 8 bits. It is also referred to as an octet.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Hex color**: A color is represented as a combination of red, green, and blue on computer systems. If one byte is assigned for each of the primary colors (red, green, and blue), we can get more than 16 million color combinations.  
* Conditionals with **if** and **else**  
* Loops with **while**

# LAN

**LAN**: Local area network, is a small private network that connects devices in one place, it lets those devices share files, printers, and internet connection quickly and security using switches/routers.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Topology** describes how devices are arranged and connected through these types…

&nbsp;

**Bus:** one main cable, connects all devices. Easy and cheap for small networks but can slow or fail if cable breaks.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Star:** all devices connected to the central hub/switch. If one device fails it does not affect others, if the central device fails then the whole network goes down.

&nbsp;

**Ring:** devices connected in a closed loop, each device passes data to the next. Predictable performance but a single break can disrupt the ring.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Switch:** is a device that connects multiple devices in a network allowing them to communicate with each other within the same local area. It forwards data only to the specific devices that needs it which helps keep the network efficient&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Router:** connects different networks together like home network to internet, it directs data between these networks and assigns IP addresses to devices helping communicate outside their local area.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Network Address**: This is the identifier for a specific network segment. It shows which devices are part of the same network. For example, in the address 192.168.1.0/24, the network address is 192.168.1.0.

&nbsp;

**Host Address**: This is the unique identifier for a device (like a computer or printer) within a network. In the address 192.168.1.5, the host address is 5, meaning it's the fifth device in that network segment.

&nbsp;

**Default Gateway**: This is the device (usually a router) that connects a local network to the internet or other networks. It helps devices on the network communicate outside of their local area. For example, if the default gateway is 192.168.1.1, that’s the address used to reach the internet from the local network.

&nbsp;

**ARP** (Address Resolution Protocol): A network protocol used to find the MAC address corresponding to an IP address on a local network. It helps devices communicate with each other by translating logical addresses (IP) into physical addresses (MAC).

&nbsp;

ARP **Request**: A message sent by a device asking, "Who has this IP address?" It broadcasts to all devices on the network to find out which one holds the specified IP.

&nbsp;

ARP **Reply**: The response from the device that has the requested IP address. It includes its MAC address, allowing the requester to establish a direct communication link.

&nbsp;

**MAC (Media Access Control) Address:** A unique identifier assigned to network interfaces for communications on the physical network. It's used to distinguish devices on the same local network.

&nbsp;

**DHCP (dynamic host configuration protocol)** is a network protocol that automatically assigns ip addresses to devices on a network, allowing them to communicate effectively and eliminate the need for manual ip address config.

&nbsp;

**Discover**: The first step where a device (client) sends a broadcast message requesting an IP address from any available DHCP server on the network.

&nbsp;

**Offer**: The DHCP server responds to the Discover message with an Offer message, which includes an available IP address and other network configuration details.

&nbsp;

**Request**: The client receives the Offer and sends back a Request message to the DHCP server, indicating that it wants to accept the offered IP address.

&nbsp;

**ACK** (Acknowledgement): The DHCP server responds with an ACK, confirming that the IP address has been assigned to the client, completing the DHCP handshake process.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# OSI model

**OSI:** Open systems interconnection is a way to understand how different network protocols work together in 7 different layers, from physical connection to application services.

&nbsp;

**Encapsulation** is the key term when pieces of info get added to data.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Network interface card (NIC)** is the name of the piece of hardware that all networked devices come with.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**OSPF:** Open shortest path first is a protocol where each router learns the whole network map and calculates the best path \*lowest cost\* to every destination.

&nbsp;

**RIP:** protocol that shares route hop counts with neighbors, picks paths with the fewest hops has a 15 hop limit best for small networks.

&nbsp;

**GUI (graphical user interface):** allows users to interact with electronic devices through graphical icons and audio indicators,

&nbsp;

**7 layers:**

![A colorful diagram of the 7 layers of the OSI model: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application, arranged in a stack from bottom to top with clear labels.][image1]

&nbsp;

1. **Physical:** shows physical components of hardware used in networking and is the lowest layer that you will find. Devices use electrical signals transfer data between each in a **binary** numbering systems 1’s and 0’s  
   &nbsp;  
2. **Data link:** is responsible for transferring data between devices on the same network using physical addresses (MAC addresses). It helps ensure that the right data gets to the right device during communication.&nbsp;  
   &nbsp;  
3. **Network:** handles routing and logical addressing (IP’s) to move packets between different networks.&nbsp;  
   &nbsp;  
4. **Transport:** When data is sent between devices, it follows one of two different protocols that are decided based upon several factors…  
   &nbsp;  
   **TCP (transmission control protocol):** designed with reliability and guarantee in mind. It reserves a constant connection between 2 devices for the amount of time it takes for the data to be sent and received.&nbsp;  
   &nbsp;  
   **UDP (user datagram protocol):** is suitable for protocols that rely on fast queries like DNS and for protocols that prioritizes real time communications such as audio/video conferencing and broadcast.  
   &nbsp;

![A comparison graphic between TCP and UDP. TCP is shown as a reliable, connection-oriented handshake with delivery confirmation. UDP is shown as a fast, connectionless transmission without delivery guarantees, like a stream of data packets.][image2]

5. **Session:** after data has been correctly formatted from the presentation layer, this layer will begin to create and maintain the connection to another computer for which the data is destined. This layer is also responsible for closing the connection if it hasn't been used for a while or is lost.&nbsp;  
   &nbsp;  
6. **Presentation:** acts as a translator for data to and from the application layer. The receiving computer will also understand data sent to a computer in one format destined for another format. Ex. when you send email, the other user may have another email client to you but contents of the email will still need to display the same.  
   &nbsp;  
7. **Application:** protocols and rules are in place to determine how the user interact with data sent or received.  
   &nbsp;

# Packets/frames

**Packet** is the name for a piece of data when it **does have** IP addressing info.

&nbsp;

**Frame** is the name for a piece of data when it does **not** have IP addressing info.

# HTTP in details

**Ranges of status codes:**

&nbsp;

**100-199 info response**: shows first part of a request is accepted and continuing sending the reset

&nbsp;

**200-299 Success**: confirms the request was successful.

&nbsp;

**300-399 Redirection**: redirects the request to another resource or webpage

&nbsp;

**400-499 Client Errors**: Indicates an error with the clients request.

&nbsp;

**500-599 Server Errors**: shows a major problem on the servers side.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**HTTP Responses**

&nbsp;

**200 OK**: request was successful&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**201 Created**: new resource created successfully&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**301 Moved permanently**: Resource has a new URL&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**302 Found**: Resource temporarily moved to a new URL&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**400 Bad request**: request was invalid or malformed

&nbsp;

**401 Unauthorized**: authentication required

&nbsp;

**403 Forbidden**: Access denied to the resource

&nbsp;

**404 Not found**: Resource not found

&nbsp;

**500 Internal server error**: server encountered an error.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**503 Service unavailable:** this server cannot handle your request as its either overloaded or down for maintenance.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Common request header:**&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Host:** the domain name of the server

&nbsp;

**User-agent:** info about the client browser or application

&nbsp;

**Content-length:** size of the request body in bytes

&nbsp;

**Accept-encoding:** accepted content encodings (gzip, deflate etc.)

&nbsp;

**Cookie:** stored cookies sent to server

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Common Response headers:**

&nbsp;

**Set-Cookie:** Cookie sent by the server to be stored by client&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Cache-control:** controls for caching behaviour&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Content-Type** media type of the returned content

&nbsp;

**Content- Encoding:** encoding used on the response body eg. gzip

# Networking basics

**Volunteered data \-**  this is created and shared by individuals such as network profiles and might include video files, pictures, text or audio files.

&nbsp;

**Observed data-** this is captured by recording the actions of individuals such as location data when using a cell phone.

&nbsp;

**Inferred data \-** this is data such as credit score which is based on analysis of volunteered or observed data.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**3 common signal transmission used in networks:**

&nbsp;

**Electrical signals \-** transmission is achieved&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Optical signals-** transmission is achieved by converting the electrical signals into light pulses&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Wireless signals \-** transmission is achieved by using infrared, microwave, or radio waves through the air.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Bandwidth** is the capacity of a medium to carry data. Digital bandwidth measures rhe amount of data that can flow from one place to another in a given amount of time. Common bandwidth measurement follows as**…**

&nbsp;

* Thousands of bits per second (Kbps)  
* Million of bits per second (Mbps)  
* Billions of bits per second (Gbps)

&nbsp;

**Latency** refers to the amount of time, including delays, for data to travel from given point to another.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

An **actuator** is a mechanical or electromechanical device that converts an energy source into controlled physical motion&nbsp;

# how the web works

**CDN (content delivery networks)** can be used to host static files and speed up a client's visit to a site.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**The load balancer** performs a **health check** to make sure the host is still alive.

&nbsp;

**WAF (web application firewall**) can be used to help against the hacking of a website.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

A **load balancer** is a tool that helps distribute incoming network traffic across multiple servers, making sure no single server gets overwhelmed and that all users have a faster, more reliable experience.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

**Virtual hosts** is used by web server software to host multiple sites

# CIA triad

There are 3 pillars of the **CIA Triad…**

&nbsp;

1. **Confidentiality**  
   Ensuring digital information is not available to unauthorized individuals.  
   &nbsp;  
2. **Integrity**  
   Ensuring digital information is not modified without permission.  
   &nbsp;  
3. **Availability**  
   Ensuring digital information is not unavailable when needed.  
   &nbsp;

# Cryptography concepts

**Plaintext** is what you can read. **Ciphertext** is the scrambled gibberish.

&nbsp;

A **key** is the secret that controls scrambling and unscrambling.’

&nbsp;

**2 types of encryption:**

&nbsp;

- **Symmetric:** uses a single key for both encryption and decryption. Its fast and efficient, but you need a secure way to share that key.&nbsp;  
  &nbsp;  
- **Asymmetric:** uses 2 linked keys, a public key that anyone can use and a private key for one person to keep. This solves distribution problems and powers initial handshake for https connections.

&nbsp;

**Asymmetric**  sets up shared key at the start

**symmetric** handles the actual data because its faster

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# Become a hacker terminology

* **Scope**: The rules that say what can and cannot be tested during a security check.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Vulnerability**: A flaw or hole in a system that makes it possible for someone to break in.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Exploit**: A specific tool or trick used to take advantage of a vulnerability.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Enumeration**: Creating a list of everything on a system to find the easiest way in.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Credentials**: Information like usernames and passwords used to prove who you are.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Authentication**: The process of verifying that a user really is who they say they are.  
  &nbsp;  
* **Dictionary attack**: A way to guess passwords by trying every word from a long list.

&nbsp;

# Crontab values

A crontab is simply a special file with formatting that is recognised by the cron process to execute each line step-by-step. Crontabs require 6 specific values:

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| Value | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| MIN | What minute to execute at |
| HOUR | What hour to execute at |
| DOM | What day of the month to execute at |
| MON | What month of the year to execute at |
| DOW | What day of the week to execute at |
| CMD | The actual command that will be executed. |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# microsoft fundamentals

**NTFS** (new technology file system) is known as a journaling file system, in case of failure, the file system can automatically repair the folders on disk using info stored in a log file. This function is not available without **FAT**

&nbsp;

Before **NTFS** there was **FAT16/FAT32**  (file allocation table) and **HPFS** (high performance file system)

&nbsp;

**System32** is located at  local disk – windows file – system32 holds important files for os
